ops-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGER: High latency observed on /v1/generate in us-west-2. Alerting policies triggered: p95 > 1s for 5m. Root time=2026-03-15T15:06:42Z

maya: I’m paged. seeing big jump around 15:06 UTC, coincides with kernel rollout to worker pool A. p50 went from ~180ms -> 260ms, p95 from ~480ms -> ~1.2s. CPU % looks fine.

devon: oncall here, joining. any customer-facing degradation?

sam: A few customers reported slow streaming responses, some timeouts at 30s. We're throttling retries but still seeing elevated error budget.

maya: quick timeline:
- 14:58 UTC: canary of kernel 5.17.14+redwood-rc deployed to pool A (canary 5 hosts)
- 15:02 UTC: rollout started to remaining hosts in pool A
- 15:06 UTC: metrics jump (p95 spike)
- 15:09 UTC: alerts trigger

cheng: copying kernel info from one affected host:
```
$ uname -a
Linux worker-A-23 5.17.14+redwood-rc #27 SMP PREEMPT Tue Mar 15 14:45:01 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

elliot: I grabbed a perf stat for the model server PID 2419 on affected host:
```
$ sudo perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-cycles,cycles:u,instructions -p 2419 sleep 5
 Performance counter stats for 'sleep 5':
    1,495,612 context-switches
  2,345,123,456 cpu-cycles
  1,123,456,789 cycles:u
    987,654,321 instructions
  5.012345678 seconds time elapsed
```

maya: that context-switches number is way up vs baseline (~120k over same interval). suggests scheduling churn. also seeing long wait_for_completion spans in traces.

sam: can you paste a trace snippet?

maya: trace spans (otel) from a slow request:
```
span: request /v1/generate id=trace-8f3a
  - service: runtime-step (duration 1.18s)
  - child span: tokenizer (12ms)
  - child span: kernel-syscall wait (890ms) tag=io_wait
  - child span: kv-cache lookup (8ms)
```

devon: kernel-syscall wait 890ms is suspicious. could be sched latency or blocking syscall in driver. any I/O saturation? iostat shows modest disk write.

cheng: NIC driver version matches previous, no recent driver roll. only kernel config change in this build was enabling PREEMPT_RCU and a scheduler tweak (CONFIG_SCHED_AUTOGROUP changes). build tag: kc/5.17.14-redwood-rc#27 (commit abcdef1234).

elliot: collecting dmesg + stack traces from a wedged worker, dropping them here:
```
[Mar15 15:07:12] worker-A-23 kernel: scheduling: high latency detected: task=runtime-step pid=2419 blocked for 870ms
[Mar15 15:07:12] stack: schedule+0x1b3/0x260
[Mar15 15:07:12] stack: vma_fault+0x45/0xc0
[Mar15 15:07:12] stack: handle_mm_fault+0x3a0/0x6b0
```

maya: hypothesis 1: scheduler/preempt changes in this kernel are increasing context-switches under our workload (many small actor tasks + continuous batching), causing p95 to blow up.

sam: hypothesis 2: KV cache lock contention amplified by kernel timing changes -> long syscall waits.

devon: immediate mitigation options? rollback kernel or drain pool A and reroute traffic. rolling back whole fleet would be noisy.

maya: I’m going to reroute traffic away from pool A to pool B (legacy kernel) for incoming inference traffic. updating router now.

ellisot: paste router command?

maya:
```
# update routing weight for poolA -> 0
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/route/update \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","weights":{"poolA":0,"poolB":100}}'
```

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Route update accepted. poolB now at 100% for /v1/generate in us-west-2.

cheng: routing switch confirmed at loadbalancer logs 15:11:03Z.

sam: seeing p95 drop starting 15:12 UTC on affected metric—p95 back to ~520ms, p50 ~200ms. still slightly above baseline but much better.

devon: good. let’s keep poolA drained for now and avoid kernel rollout until RCA. we should also capture perf/top profiles under controlled load for older vs new kernel.

maya: agreed. plan:
- keep poolA out of rotation + pause kernel rollout (actioned)
- collect perf samples and ftrace on an isolated host reproduced under load (maya, elliot)
- gather full set of traces and compare span timings (cheng)

elliot: starting perf script to collect off-CPU stacks and sched wakeups:
```
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60
sudo perf report --stdio > /tmp/perf-report-poolA.txt
```

cheng: also collecting BPF trace for sched_events, will upload to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2501357902/sched-bpf.log

maya: customer impact update: 7 customers reported intermittent slow responses, 2 had degraded SLAs. CS notified at 15:20 UTC.

sam: adding hypotheses to tracker: (1) scheduler config change -> increased context switches -> syscall stalls. (2) KV-cache lock contention exacerbated by scheduling. (3) driver/firmware edge case unlikely but keep open. evidence: perf context-switch spike, dmesg scheduling warnings, kernel commit includes sched autogroup change.

devon: next steps owner map:
- perf and offcpu flamegraphs: elliot (ETA 60m)
- kernel config diff + build notes: cheng (ETA 30m)
- routing/drain verification + rollback playbook: maya (in progress)
- customer comms draft: sam (ETA 45m)

maya: I'm handing off incident to devon for follow-up. devon has the pager and will coordinate RCA doc. :handshake:

devon: taking over. will open an RCA doc and attach logs. please upload perf outputs and BPF traces to the incident S3 path. leave any stray notes here.

elliot: uploaded perf report and preliminary flamegraphs: https://s3.redwood/internal/2501357902/perf-flamegraphs.html

cheng: kernel config diff gist: https://gist.github.com/cheng/abcdef1234 (highlights PREEMPT_RCU and CONFIG_SCHED_AUTOGROUP changes)

devon: initial mitigation effective. marking incident status: mitigated -> degraded. will reconvene after perf analysis to decide rollback vs kernel patch.

maya: one more data point: in controlled repro with new kernel, tail latency distribution shows a heavy tail; sampling shows many requests blocked in schedule+0x1b3. attaching sample stacks in thread.

sam: good work team. keep running captures. I'll coordinate CS comms and post an update at +1h.

ops-bot: :spiral_notepad: Incident note saved (id=INC-2501357902). Handoff: maya -> devon.

devon: logging hypotheses in RCA tracker:
- H1: scheduler change caused increased preemption/context-switching -> higher p95. (evidence: perf/context-switches, dmesg scheduling warnings, kernel diff)
- H2: locking/contended paths in runtime exposed by timing change. (evidence: trace span long kernel-syscall wait, KV lock reports)
- H3: unrelated driver/firmware regression (low confidence).

devon: closing immediate paging. will reopen if metrics regress after draining.

maya: thanks everyone, transferring any remaining notes to RCA doc.
